package_info.package_name: Blender Photo Editor-Easy Photo Background Editor
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions available at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: The app contains embedded malicious code that steals users’ Facebook credentials and abuses them to run unauthorized ad campaigns using the victim’s payment information. This constitutes credential theft and financial fraud, making the entire package malicious.

execution_context.file_location: Android app code (likely in a Java/Kotlin class responsible for Facebook login or background service)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts Facebook login credentials entered by the user, sends them via HTTP POST to a remote attacker-controlled server, enabling credential exfiltration and subsequent account abuse.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating user credentials to an external server is a classic sign of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate photo editor app should never access or transmit Facebook credentials outside of the official Facebook SDK or authentication flow.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use Facebook login via the official SDK, but credentials are never handled directly or sent to third-party servers.
key_indicators: Direct access to Facebook login fields
Transmission of credentials to non-Facebook domains
Use of HTTP POST to unknown external server

execution_context.file_location: Android app code (background service or ad management module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After stealing credentials, the code uses the victim’s Facebook session or token to create and run ad campaigns on Facebook, charging the victim’s payment method for unauthorized ads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Using stolen credentials to run ad campaigns is a form of financial fraud and account abuse.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A photo editor app should not interact with Facebook’s ad management APIs or use user payment information for any purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only official Facebook ad management apps should create ad campaigns, and only with explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Use of Facebook API with stolen tokens
Creation of ad campaigns without user interaction
Access to or use of payment information

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious app and is prompted to log in with Facebook credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credentials are stolen and sent to attacker.

attack_chain.action: Stolen credentials are used to access the victim’s Facebook account and payment information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker creates and runs unauthorized ad campaigns, incurring charges to the victim.

behavioral_signatures: Android apps requesting Facebook credentials outside of official SDK flows
Transmission of login credentials to non-Facebook domains
Background creation of Facebook ad campaigns using user tokens
file_indicators: App code containing hardcoded external URLs for credential exfiltration
Presence of custom Facebook login forms not using official SDK
References to Facebook ad management APIs in non-advertising apps
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with Facebook during or after login
Unusual API calls to Facebook ad endpoints from non-advertising apps
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Android apps for unauthorized access to Facebook credentials and outbound network requests to unknown domains during login. Flag apps that implement custom Facebook login forms or interact with Facebook ad APIs without being ad management tools. Analyze app code for hardcoded URLs and credential handling logic.
